INTRODUCTION\n## Too complex, not intuitive\n44. It is obvious that the number of routes (whether 148 as per LTFRB or 94 as per survey) can be reduced and simplified for efficient transport operations and passenger convenience. There are far too many routes for a city with a sparse road network. Metro Manila, with a population 10 times that of Davao, has only about 500 jeepney intra-city routes.\n45. Topologically, there are several routes that are fundamentally similar – in terms of overlaps and catchment areas. For example, Puan route is a truncated version of the Toril route or that of Mintal route, with minor differences in the turning points within the CBD. The passengers on the Puan route would be no worse off, if it was deleted – or merged with the longer ones-as the other 2 routes would simply absorb the traffic.\n\n# IV. CURRENT SITUATION IN DAVAO\n## Zone of Operation\n75. In regulating tricycles-for-hire, Davao deviated from the national implementing rules and regulations issued in 1992 when the regulation of this type of public transport got devolved from the LTFRB to the LGUs. Franchises for tricycles should be for defined zones, say, a subdivision or a barangay, rather than for fixed routes. Their service character is not unlike a taxi for hire with door-to-door service rather than a jeepney running on fixed route and minimum frequencies.\n76. To improve service coverage, passenger convenience, and income potentials of tricycles, it is recommended that the city revert to the original contemplation of zone delimitations with a flat fare within the zone. With average route lengths of 2 km, there is no logic for adopting a distance-related fare matrix. Smaller-capacity models (<4 passengers) are more suited for taxi-like services. Use of larger-capacity models (up to 6 passengers) within a zone, village, or barangay means a shared taxi service.\n\n# III. DEMAND AND TECHNOLOGY OPTIONS\n## National Environmentally Sustainable Transport\n53. A more promising option is to introduce electric or hybrid buses. At present, the capital cost is higher than diesel-powered units compliant with Euro II standard, but very competitive with Euro IV-compliant buses. Considering the higher cost of petrol fuel and lower electricity tariff in Davao City compared to Manila, it may be more economical in the long run. The indicative cost for battery-run buses is PHP6.00 per bus-kilometer against PHP16 for diesel-run vehicles. An evaluation of hybrid buses is also recommended before a final decision on the best technology for Davao’s BRT system is reached.\n55. Based on the above, large and high-capacity buses (e.g., articulated buses and/or double-deck buses) and vehicles that are not low-emission diesel (i.e., Euro V standard or above) would be excluded from further consideration.\n\n# V. INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK\n## E. Past Proposals from Past BRT Studies for Metro Manila and Cebu\n142. To date, no BRT project has been implemented in the Philippines. There is no existing and operational BRT model elsewhere in the Philippines after which the Davao BRT may be patterned. The nearest to such a system is probably the LRT of Manila, or the defunct Metro Manila Transit Corporation which used to operate buses.\n\n# II. SUSTAINABLE URBAN TRANSPORT FUND (SUTF)\n## A. Objective\n5. The main obstacle for creating such a fund is the absence of historical experience or precedents. Its financial records, however, implies that a special fund for education exists that also cover the construction of school buildings and facilities. Davao City, like other cities in the Philippines, has been inured to leaving the provision of public transport services to the private sector. It has, however, taken the obligation of constructing a common-use provincial bus terminal more than 3 decades ago and continues to operate the same. No cities in the Philippines have taken the challenge of an efficient, environment-friendly, and equitable transport as their obligation to the citizens and the community. While a mass transit system is in the LGUs radar screen, it is almost always framed as a big-ticket rail asset to be granted at no cost by (if not lobbied from) the national government. The airports are organized, signs are in English, and everything is clearly marked, so even first time Filipino travelers will feel comfortable. From the airport, you can choose between train, bus, taxi, or private transfer, making your ride to the city smooth and simple after a long flight.\n\n❤️Pro Tip: When planning your visit, consider booking [**flights from Manila to Tokyo**](https://ph.trip.com/flights/manila-to-tokyo/airfares-mnl-tyo/) and [**Tokyo hotels**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotels-list-228/) in advance to secure the best rates.\n\nHotels & homes\n\n3-Night Stay Discount\n\n3 night stays: Tiered savings (up to 6% off). Preparing your documents early helps you avoid delays and makes arrival in Seoul much smoother.\n\n## Tokyo Airport Train: Easy Way to Reach the City\n\nTaking the train from Tokyo airports is simple and very organized. Trains are on time, stations are clean, and signs are clear in English. If you are used to MRT in Manila, this feels more structured and less stressful, even during rush hour.\n\n### From Narita Airport\n\n![Narita Aiport](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/0M75012000r7ts9ww307E.png?proc=format/f_webp)\n\n_Sources: narita-airport.jp_\n\n#### 🛤️ **Narita Express NEX**\n\n**Location:** JR Station B1 level\n\n##### Route Details\n\nNarita Terminal 1 or 2 → Tokyo Station → Shinagawa → Shibuya → Shinjuku → Ikebukuro\n\n##### ⏱ Travel Time\n\n- Around 60 minutes to Tokyo Station\n- Around 80 to 90 minutes to Shinjuku\n\n##### 💸 Cost\n\n¥3,200 to ¥5,000 (₱1,200 to ₱1,850)\n\nBest for travelers staying near Tokyo Station, Shinjuku, Shibuya, or Ikebukuro who want a direct ride with luggage space.\n\n#### 🛤️ **Keisei Skyliner**\n\n**Location:** Keisei Station B1 level\n\n##### Route Details\n\nNarita → Nippori → Keisei Ueno\n\nFrom Nippori, transfer to the JR Yamanote Line going to Ueno, Tokyo, Akihabara, Ikebukuro, Shinjuku, and Shibuya.\n\n##### ⏱ Travel Time\n\n40 to 50 minutes to Nippori\n\n##### 💸 Cost\n\n¥2,580 (₱950)\n\n**💡 Important tip for Filipino travelers with heavy luggage**\n\nTransfer at Nippori instead of Ueno. At Nippori, the transfer to JR Yamanote Line is only about a 2 minute walk on the same level using a dedicated transfer gate. Ueno requires longer walking and can be more tiring.\n\nFor many staying in Ikebukuro or Shinjuku, Skyliner plus Yamanote is often faster and cheaper than NEX.\n\n#### 🛤️ **Local Train from Narita Airport**\n\n**Location:** B1 level at Narita Airport, follow signs for JR Line or Keisei Line\n\nIf you want the cheapest way to reach Tokyo, taking a regular commuter train is a good option. These are not airport express trains, but normal city trains used by locals every day.\n\n##### Detailed Route Options\n\n###### **JR Sobu Line Rapid**\n\nNarita Airport → Chiba → Tokyo Station\n\nThis goes directly to Tokyo Station without transfers. From Tokyo Station, you can change to JR Yamanote Line for Ueno, Shinjuku, or Shibuya.\n\n###### **Keisei Main Line**\n\nNarita Airport → Nippori\n\nAt Nippori, transfer to JR Yamanote Line going to Ueno, Tokyo, Ikebukuro, Shinjuku, and Shibuya.\n\n##### ⏱ Travel Time\n\nAround 70 to 110 minutes depending on traffic and your final stop.\n\n##### 💸 Cost\n\n¥1,050 to ¥1,350 (around ₱390 to ₱500).\n\n### JR Pass for All Japan Rail Travel\n\nEnjoy unlimited travel around Japan with the JR Pass, covering JR Shinkansen, buses, and ferries. It also includes free EMS shipping. Orders placed before 11:00 AM on weekdays will be shipped on the same day.\n\n**Best For:** Multi-city Japan trips\n\n**Shipping:** Free EMS shipping\n\n**Good to Know:** Same-day shipping for weekday orders before 11:00 AM\n\n![JR](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images//0586b12000sn25byo446C_C_1080_540_Q80.jpg_.webp)\n\nJR Pass (all Japan 7/14/21-day rail pass)\n\nInstant confirmation\n\nFree global EMS shipping\n\nFrom PHP 18,835.41\n\n[Book Now](https://ph.trip.com/things-to-do/detail/107992260/)\n\nTrains\n\n5% off Japan Rail new user promo code\n\nCopy\n\n> 📌 **Booking Tip:** Get **5% off Japan Railway bookings** with this new user promo code. Valid for JR lines, including Shinkansen and Limited Express. **JR Pass not included.**\n\n### From Haneda Airport\n\n![Haneda Airport](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/0M72t12000rapeehsA5BE_Q60.jpg?proc=format/f_webp)\n\n_Sources: tokyo-haneda.com_\n\n#### 🛤️ **Keikyu Line**\n\n**Location:** Terminal 3 B1 level\n\n##### Route Details\n\n- Haneda → Shinagawa\n\nSome trains are Airport Limited Express. These continue directly into the Toei Asakusa Subway Line\n\n- Haneda → Shinagawa → Sengakuji → Higashi Ginza → Nihombashi → Asakusa\n\nIf your hotel is in Ginza, Nihombashi, or Asakusa, you may not need to transfer. You simply stay on the train.\n\n##### ⏱ Travel Time\n\n- 15 to 20 minutes to Shinagawa\n- Around 30 minutes to Asakusa\n\n##### 💸 Cost\n\n¥330 to ¥550 (₱120 to ₱200)\n\nThis is usually the most practical and budget friendly option from Haneda.\n\n#### 🛤️ **Tokyo Monorail**\n\n**Location:** Terminal 3 3F\n\n##### Route Details\n\nHaneda → Tennozu Isle → Hamamatsucho\n\nFrom Hamamatsucho, transfer to JR Yamanote Line for Tokyo, Ueno, Shinjuku, and Shibuya.\n\n##### ⏱ Travel Time\n\n13 to 20 minutes\n\n##### 💸 Cost\n\n¥500 to ¥750 (₱185 to ₱280)\n\nGood choice if staying around Minato area or near Tokyo Bay. You also get nice water views along the way.\n\nHotels & homes\n\n3-Night Stay Discount\n\n3 night stays: Tiered savings (up to 6% off). Narita.\n\n### 🧳 Luggage Rule\n\n- This bus has a strict rule of **one large suitcase per person** for the luggage compartment.\n- If you bring two big suitcases or large balikbayan boxes, staff may ask you to pay for an extra seat or may refuse boarding if the bus is full.\n- If you are traveling with many big bags, consider Narita Express instead.\n\n👍 **Pro Tip**: Don’t forget to look for Staff will help you get a taxi.\n\nYou can also book through ride-hailing apps.\n\n### 📱 Ride-Hailing Apps\n\n- **Uber** – Available in Tokyo, often dispatches regular taxis\n- **GO App** – One of the most common taxi apps in Japan\n- **S.RIDE** – Another local taxi booking app\n\n### 💸 Estimated Fare\n\n| Route | Approx. Transfer](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0352z120009jwh11k537D_C_1080_607.jpg_.webp)\n\nA private airport transfer is a comfortable option if you want a **direct ride from the airport to your hotel** without train transfers. It is popular for families, groups, or travelers with heavy luggage.\n\n### 🕒 Travel Time\n\n- **Haneda Airport → Tokyo:** about **30–50 minutes**\n- **Narita Airport → Tokyo:** about **60–90 minutes**\n\nPrivate transfers are usually **available 24 hours**, and drivers typically meet passengers at the airport arrival area.\n\n### 💸 Estimated Price\n\n| Vehicle Type | Approx. Cost | Best For |\n| Standard Car | about **₱3,000–₱4,000** | Solo travelers or couples |\n| Van | about **₱4,500–₱6,000** | Families or small groups |\n\n### 📱 Where to Book\n\nPrivate transfers can be booked in advance through platforms such as **Trip.com or other airport transfer services**.\n\n### 🧳 Best For\n\n- Families or groups\n- Travelers with large luggage\n- Late-night or early-morning arrivals\n- Hotels far from train stations\n\n### ⚠️ Things to Know\n\n- Usually **more expensive than train or airport bus**\n- **Advance booking is recommended**\n\n## Secure Your Stay in Tokyo\n\n![Hotel New Otani Tokyo Garden Tower](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0202a12000a0oy5vo81AC_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Hotel New Otani Tokyo Garden Tower**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-2143741/hotel-new-otani-tokyo-garden-tower/ \"Hotel New Otani Tokyo Garden Tower\")\n\n9.3 _/10_Great839 Reviews\n\nCentral Tokyo Tokyo _\\|_ 2.87km from city center\n\nThe hotel's location and surroundings are excellent. The only minor inconvenience was having to walk all the way around to access the garden downstairs; I'm not sure if we just missed a more direct entrance. On our second day in Tokyo, we experienced a typhoon with strong winds and heavy rain, but the soundproofing in the room was so good we couldn't hear a thing – it was incredibly quiet. Getting around was also very convenient, as it's close to the subway station, making it easy to reach popular areas like Shinjuku, Shibuya, and Ginza.\n\nFromPHP 16,616\n\n![Mitsui Garden Hotel Ginza Premier](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc5612000i3u0bvqFD8A_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Mitsui Garden Hotel Ginza Premier**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-688381/mitsui-garden-hotel-ginza-premier/ \"Mitsui Garden Hotel Ginza Premier\")\n\n9.1 _/10_Great1365 Reviews\n\nGinza/Tsukiji Tokyo _\\|_ 0.49km from city center\n\nHighly recommend the Mitsui Garden Hotel Ginza Premier in Tokyo! The room offered an amazing view, perfect for enjoying the bustling city lights at night. It's just a few minutes' walk to Shimbashi Station, making it super convenient for getting around and shopping. The sky lobby is quite unique, service communication was smooth, and the room was clean and tidy. Its Ginza location makes shopping and dining effortless. Definitely my top choice for a Tokyo trip.\n\nFromPHP 16,654\n\n![Imperial Hotel, Tokyo](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc0t12000aq58ryl3E78_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Imperial Hotel, Tokyo**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-993510/imperial-hotel-tokyo/ \"Imperial Hotel, Tokyo\")\n\n9.5 _/10_Amazing2530 Reviews\n\nGinza/Tsukiji Tokyo _\\|_ 0.66km from city center\n\nI really hope you take a look, I think it might be helpful to you.\n(Good morning, good afternoon, good evening to you all) (Note: The pictures mainly feature food)\n\nThis is my third stay at the Imperial Hotel Tokyo (the first 2 times were booked by my mom). (I just turned 15).\n\nThe hotel changes bedding daily, cleans meticulously, and the service is warm and friendly.\n\nThe breakfast restaurant offers many options 🤔.\n\nAlso, there's a Yakiniku restaurant (Jojoen) very close behind the hotel, which is rarely crowded. I've eaten there many times (sometimes even on weekend evenings) and never had to wait for a table.\n(Was I just lucky?)\n\nThe pictures I've included are all from the hotel. I haven't included Jojoen, but it's definitely worth a try!\n\nP8 shows the signature dish (beef) from the hotel's buffet dinner. The beef is juicy and flavorful, tender but not mushy, and the sauce is the perfect touch. (I thought the potatoes were delicious, and by the way, is that white blob garlic?! It's horseradish!)\n\nP4 and P5 show two different main dishes from the Japanese-style breakfast (you can choose porridge instead of rice). (Sometimes the ingredients change; I once encountered a time when there was no salmon, but the taste was still excellent) 🤔.\n\nOh, and the pancakes are absolutely amazing! So good I forgot to take pictures (maybe not that good?), but the aroma is incredible!!!!\n\n(Note: Most restaurants in Japan will ask you if you have any food allergies. Don't panic if you're asked; just answer truthfully. ”Allergy” is the common word used for this.)\n\nThe hotel staff's English proficiency is really good! Seriously!\n\nSeiyoken + Din Tai Fung + Ichiran ads passing by...\n\nYou can try Seiyoken. It's very famous and has been around for a long time. I've tried their full meals (both the grill and the cafe, emmm... the grill's main dishes were quite impressive, as for the cafe, I thought it was decent. Their signature beef stew, though the meat chunks are large, is really soft, flavorful, and fragrant! The other dishes were also quite good. Oh, and definitely get their Duck Farm Pudding to go before you leave! It's fantastic!!!!! The caramel is a bit bitter, which I personally don't mind).\n\nThe Imperial Hotel's omurice (omelet rice) is good.\n\nRoom service is quite special! You can do almost everything in the room with just one tablet, such as ordering room service, checking breakfast queue status, closing curtains, and turning off lights.\n\nThat's about it. My opinion on Kamon is that it's worth trying once.\n\n(Most of the above-mentioned Imperial Hotel restaurants are more budget-friendly if you choose lunch options).\n\nTo the hotel, I'd say you've done a great job. There's nothing to pick apart. Many of the services are very detailed. Negative reviews do exist, but I honestly didn't notice any... (that's on me). Also, a good travel mood is very important. This is just my review. Wishing you a pleasant journey!\n\nThe hotel staff is very helpful! They will solve problems for you. Last time, my mom thought the indoor lighting wasn't perfect? If you’re hoping to explore and enjoy the local food culture in Japan, I personally wouldn’t recommend including breakfast at the hotel, as there are plenty of other food options around to try.\n\nFromPHP 7,958\n\n![Aman Tokyo](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/220i0z000000mqedk3EB4_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Aman Tokyo**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-2479231/aman-tokyo/ \"Aman Tokyo\")\n\n9.6 _/10_Amazing158 Reviews\n\nTokyo Station/Nihonbashi Tokyo _\\|_ 1.59km from city center\n\nIt was 5:30 PM in Otemachi, Tokyo, and a massive halo, like a holy light, enveloped the area, reflecting the silhouette of the world's most beautiful CBD on the glass facade of Otemachi Tower. Perched atop this magnificent skyscraper, Aman Tokyo, which stunned the world a decade ago, remains an unparalleled benchmark for modern city hotels.\n\n｜The soaring 30-meter high atrium, crafted with washi lanterns, wood textures, and concrete and rock, creates a 'dry landscape' garden in the urban clouds.\n｜The view facing the Imperial Palace is arguably Tokyo's most beautiful skyline (it ruthlessly trumps the already impressive view from the neighboring Bulgari).\n｜While the ambiance at Arva, the Italian restaurant on the other side of the lobby, is superb, the food wasn't to my taste. I'd recommend the Aman Cafe on the first floor, a glasshouse enveloped by the 'Otemachi Forest' oasis instead.\n\nFromPHP 220,153\n\n![HOSHINOYA Tokyo](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0221c12000kzu3m6pF9EE_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**HOSHINOYA Tokyo**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-6372841/hoshinoya-tokyo/ \"HOSHINOYA Tokyo\")\n\n9 _/10_Great89 Reviews\n\nTokyo Station/Nihonbashi Tokyo _\\|_ 1.84km from city center\n\n\\[HOSHINOYA Tokyo: A Vertical Ryokan Experience\\]\nHOSHINOYA Tokyo offers a truly unique concept. It is a traditional Japanese ryokan built vertically within a modern skyscraper, located in the prestigious Otemachi district. It provides a serene, luxurious escape right in the middle of the bustling city, perfectly blending classic ryokan hospitality with world-class modern design. We enjoyed a wonderful three-day, two-night stay at the property from 29 May to 31 May. We chose not to make any meal reservations, which gave us the flexibility to simply relax and explore the surrounding city.\n\n\\[Getting There\\]\nWe travelled from Fufu Hakone via a day trip to Enoshima and Kamakura. We took a direct train from Kamakura to Tokyo Station, followed by a short walk to the hotel, and arrived at around 8:00 PM. To make the transit completely effortless, our luggage was picked up and delivered directly to the hotel by LuggAgent on the same day.\n\n\\[Arrival and Check-In\\]\nThe hotel is situated in the central business district and distinctly stands out from the surrounding buildings. The discreet entrance completely shields you from the busy streets. Upon entering, staff immediately store your shoes, as the entire tatami-matted building operates on a barefoot or socks-only policy. We were incredibly lucky to catch a traditional jap instrument performance, which is usually reserved for weekends. A designated staff member managed our check-in with welcome snack & tea and escorted us to level 15. A major highlight is the exclusive lounge on each floor, shared by only 6 suites. It functions as a private living room, fully stocked with complimentary seasonal teas, coffees, and traditional snacks.\n\n\\[The Suite\\]\nWe stayed in the Sakura suite. Rather than trying to describe the beautiful layout in words, I will let my photos speak for themselves. The beds are low to the floor with a mid-level hardness that we found quite comfortable, and each bed comes with two soft pillows. There is also a television cleverly hidden behind a mirror, though it is worth noting that it only broadcasts Japanese channels. We kept it switched off to maintain the consistent traditional ryokan feel. The provided yukata is absolutely superb. It comes as a full set complete with an inner layer, an outer layer, socks, and a small handbag. The material is soft, stretchy, and incredibly comfortable for lounging and walking around the property.\n\n\\[The Top-Floor Onsen\\]\nHaving a natural hot spring in central Tokyo is a rare luxury. The onsen is located on the 17th floor and features a stunning design where the roof is open to the sky. As cameras are strictly prohibited, you will have to visualise it or check the hotel website for gallery photos. I understand that the bath is a salty hot spring containing a high concentration of seawater and seaweed minerals trapped deep in the ground. Soaking in this soothing water gently embraces the skin and helps alleviate fatigue in both body and mind. The onsen is open daily from 3:00 PM to 11:30 AM. It was the absolute perfect way to warm up and recharge before we headed out for a busy day.\n\n\\[Areas for Improvement\\]\nToothbrush Set: The provided toothbrush is far too small and takes ages to use. Being able to relax in an outdoor bath right in the center of Tokyo while looking out at the city was an amazing experience.\nThe breakfast was also very good.\n\nFromPHP 15,753\n\n![Onyado Nono Asakusa Natural Hot Spring](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0220x12000a8y835cFBF4_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Onyado Nono Asakusa Natural Hot Spring**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-37973913/onyado-nono-asakusa-natural-hot-spring/ \"Onyado Nono Asakusa Natural Hot Spring\")\n\n9 _/10_Great718 Reviews\n\nUeno/Asakusa Tokyo _\\|_ 5.55km from city center\n\nThe room was a bit small, and there was no Chinese-speaking staff, which made us feel a bit overlooked as Chinese guests.\n\nHowever, the night-time noodles were as delicious as always, and the breakfast was very authentic Japanese.\n\nThe hotel is very close to Senso-ji Temple, which allowed us to visit during off-peak hours and avoid the crowds.\n\nFromPHP 8,610\n\n![Villa Fontaine Grand Tokyo Ariake](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc0j12000cn9zmdi7BD3_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Villa Fontaine Grand Tokyo Ariake**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-49507702/hotel-villa-fontaine-grand-tokyo-ariake/ \"Villa Fontaine Grand Tokyo Ariake\")\n\n9 _/10_Great2104 Reviews\n\nOdaiba Tokyo _\\|_ 4.46km from city center\n\nThis is our second time staying here. The hotel is right next to the Ariake Garden mall, practically seamlessly connected. There are plenty of dining options upstairs and shopping is very convenient. Downstairs, there's a large Aeon supermarket, and right outside its exit, at platform 1, you can catch the bus to Haneda Airport. There's also a big Muji store nearby. Whether using Apple or Huawei devices, the experience was awful and completely mismatched with the hotel's upscale overall style.\n\nFromPHP 13,576\n\n![Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc3i12000sp6rz8lF892_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-1329588/four-seasons-hotel-tokyo-at-marunouchi/ \"Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi\")\n\n9.5 _/10_Amazing48 Reviews\n\nTokyo Station/Nihonbashi Tokyo _\\|_ 0.78km from city center\n\nI've stayed at several luxury/5 star hotels in Tokyo and Four Seasons at Marunouchi is a very rare hotel that impressed me with their service. 10/10 would recommend this to friends visiting Tokyo for a holiday.\nI filled up the arrival details form before my flight. But when I was at the airport at 8am I received an email informing me that my room was ready. I wondered if it really was as this is the first time I ever received this personalised notification. But true enough when I arrived I was brought to the lobby sofa to have a seat and was offered a glass of wine. Thereafter a staff brought me to my room to do my check in in the room itself which I thought was nice since I wouldn't need to stand at the counter. The staff also showed me around the room during check in which also included some mandarin oranges and a handwritten card which I appreciate. I was also introduced to the hotel's various message apps with the staff which I used to enquire about breakfast, spa and taxis - I found this really convenient, other hotels do not have this service. The staff who checked me in also offered to add to my personalized profile about my usual request for extra bathroom towels. Also, a heads-up: the front desk is on the 7th floor, but there's a hotel sign on the ground floor for taxi drop-offs.\n\nSince the hotel is right by Tokyo Station, you have easy access to all sorts of food, drinks, and shopping, which is why I didn't bother with the hotel breakfast. This design makes the bathroom feel quite spacious, even if the room itself is on the smaller side. A truly wonderful and delightful hotel experience.\n\nFromPHP 40,757\n\n![Grand Nikko Tokyo Daiba](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc4o12000k2ysozrFB46_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Grand Nikko Tokyo Daiba**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-759807/grand-nikko-tokyo-daiba/ \"Grand Nikko Tokyo Daiba\")\n\n9.4 _/10_Amazing1818 Reviews\n\nOdaiba Tokyo _\\|_ 5.16km from city center\n\nThe hotel's location is excellent; you can see it right after exiting Odaiba Station on the Yurikamome Line. On top of that, the vibrant izakayas surrounding the hotel were so inviting that I wished I could visit them all.\nWithout a doubt, I will choose this hotel again for my next trip to Tokyo.\nThank you once again to the entire team for a memorable stay.\n\nFromPHP 18,130\n\n![Royal Park Hotel](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc3c12000b6j31750801_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Royal Park Hotel**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-688661/royal-park-hotel/ \"Royal Park Hotel\")\n\n9.2 _/10_Great1265 Reviews\n\nTokyo Station/Nihonbashi Tokyo _\\|_ 2.31km from city center\n\nThe hotel's location is absolutely fantastic, right next to the subway station and the airport bus stop, making travel incredibly convenient. My favorite part, though, was walking into the hotel and being greeted by that unique Shangri-La scent. 🥰 And breakfast? It was a delicious five-star experience! 😋\n\nFromPHP 60,527\n\n![The Capitol Hotel Tokyu](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc1912000bxb0ziuE6FC_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**The Capitol Hotel Tokyu**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-994636/the-capitol-hotel-tokyu-tokyo/ \"The Capitol Hotel Tokyu\")\n\n9.5 _/10_Amazing186 Reviews\n\nCentral Tokyo Tokyo _\\|_ 2.21km from city center\n\nI come to Tokyo several times a year, staying a fortnight or more each time. This time I spent seven nights at The Capitol Hotel Tokyu.\n\nThe room faced Hie Shrine. Through the floor-to-ceiling windows I could see the shrine's copper roof and half of Tokyo's skyline. The décor was modern without excess; the layout flowed easily, Bose speakers hidden in the walls, another set in the bathroom ceiling, connected by a 3.5mm jack. The curtains were motorized, though you hardly needed to close them.\n\nThe turndown service. I would leave in the evening and return late to find the room changed: only the hallway light and bedside lamp left on, a bottle of water and a glass on the nightstand, two chocolates beside them. The evening tea and teacup, previously stored in the cabinet, had been moved next to the coffee machine. These changes were so slight you had to think back carefully to confirm they had happened at all. The temperature and humidity had been adjusted. As if the room itself remembered your habits.\n\nRoom service fell short of the ryokan in Hakone or Lake Toya, but well above the ordinary hotel. Each day I made two or three cups of complimentary coffee, played music, read, wrote. In seven days I finished three books. The research ahead began to take shape.\n\nThere were drawbacks. No washing machine, but a decent laundromat ten minutes' walk away—a chance to wander the streets of Akasaka. The room provided HDMI and ethernet ports but no cables; for those who came to rest, perhaps a mercy. The minibar fridge was mostly occupied by drinks for purchase, same as the Imperial, though there was still room for my sparkling water.\n\nThe day I left it was half past five and fully dark. I could barely make out the faces of the bellhop and the taxi driver. Together they loaded my luggage into the boot. I wished the bellhop a happy new year in Japanese and told her I liked her hat. She smiled and returned the greeting. As the taxi pulled out of the underground drive, I thought of the inns Kawabata once wrote about: what had to be sought in the mountains of snow country can now be reached by elevator from the B2 exit of a metro station.\n\nI have watched the Shinagawa Prince Hotel loosen quietly over time, slip a little. That kind of decline is rarely one great error. It begins the day someone forgets to leave a glass of water, neglects to move a packet of tea, omits a newspaper. As for The Capitol Hotel Tokyu: in Japanese, what I experienced over these seven days is called ちょうどいい.\n\nFromPHP 43,020\n\n![Hyatt Regency Tokyo](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mc4g12000orn7osnEC03_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Hyatt Regency Tokyo**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-994617/hyatt-regency-tokyo/ \"Hyatt Regency Tokyo\")\n\n9.1 _/10_Great769 Reviews\n\nShinjuku Area Tokyo _\\|_ 7.01km from city center\n\nOur family trip to the Hyatt Regency Tokyo was a fantastic experience overall! The location is super convenient, making it easy to get around for shopping and sightseeing. We booked a city-view king room, and the view was great. The room was clean, tidy, and well-equipped. For a Tokyo hotel, the space was quite generous, so it didn't feel cramped with the kids. The hotel lobby had a wonderful ambiance, and the staff were polite, attentive, and responsive to our needs. The cleanliness was spot on, and the bedding was comfortable, leading to a very peaceful night's sleep. The hotel facilities are excellent, and the overall atmosphere is quiet and comfortable. It's a great choice for families, perfect for both exploring and relaxing. It's definitely worth considering for a trip to Tokyo, and we'd think about staying here again next time.\n\nFromPHP 26,644\n\n![Agora Tokyo Ginza](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0226112000a6ufryw4255_R_550_412_R5.jpg)\n\n[**Agora Tokyo Ginza**](https://ph.trip.com/hotels/tokyo-hotel-detail-54566129/agora-tokyo-ginza/ \"Agora Tokyo Ginza\")\n\n8.9 _/10_Very Good292 Reviews\n\nGinza/Tsukiji Tokyo _\\|_ 0.36km from city center\n\nPros:\nthe duty manager Mai who is fluent in English and demonstrated outstanding attentiveness and a genuine dedication to hospitality. Haneda is much closer (30–45 minutes) and easier if you're staying in Tokyo. If you can, choose Haneda — it's more convenient.\n\n\n- ### What’s the cheapest way to get to the city?\n\n\n\n\n\n\nIf you're on a budget, you can take the Keisei Main Line from Narita or the Keikyu Line from Haneda. Fares start at around ₱300–₱700. These are local trains and great for backpackers or tipid travelers.\n\n\n- ### What’s the fastest way to reach Tokyo?\n\n\n\n\n\n\nFrom Narita, the Narita Express (N’EX) or Keisei Skyliner are your best bets — they’re fast, comfortable, and have space for luggage. From Haneda, take the Tokyo Monorail or Keikyu Line to reach the city quickly.\n\n\n- ### Can I use a Suica or Pasmo card?\n\n\n\n\n\n\nYes! These are IC cards that work on almost all trains, buses, and even vending machines. You can buy them at the airport and reload anytime.\n\n\n- ### Will I get lost? Are signs in English?\n\n\n\n\n\n\nDon’t worry! Tokyo is very tourist-friendly. There are English signs, clear train maps, and helpful announcements. Locals are kind too — just show your destination if you need help.\n\n\n\nDisclaimer: This article has been provided by an individual contributor or third party platform.
